thread.title_full: Review of U.S. Troop Deployment at Guantanamo Bay

author: LOLITA C. BALDOR
title: Review of U.S. Troop Deployment at Guantanamo Bay
text:
• Military officials are reviewing plans to cut the number of U.S. troops at Guantanamo Bay by as much as half.
• Currently, there are 900 troops deployed at the base.
• The review is prompted by the absence of detainees at the facility and ongoing legal challenges.
• Southern Command has been asked to provide a plan to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth regarding troop needs and space requirements.
• No migrants have been transferred to Guantanamo since early March 2025.
• At least 290 detainees have been transferred to Guantanamo since February 2025.
• On March 11, 2025, the last 40 detainees were flown from Guantanamo to Louisiana.
• The base is known for housing individuals associated with the September 11 attacks and has facilities for migrants intercepted at sea.
• President Trump has indicated plans to send 'worst criminal migrants' to Guantanamo, but civil rights attorneys argue many detainees lack criminal records.
• A recent judge's ruling against civil rights advocates was based on the current lack of migrant detainees at the base.
• The 900 troops currently stationed include approximately 500 Army soldiers, nearly 300 Marines, and several dozen sailors and airmen.
• Nearly 800 additional U.S.-based soldiers are on prepare-to-deploy orders for potential deployment to Guantanamo.
• Civil rights attorneys have filed lawsuits to prevent the transfer of migrants to Guantanamo, citing mistreatment of detainees.
• The judge expressed willingness to revisit the issue if more detainees are sent to Guantanamo in the future.
